concepts.quote: r <= sum would work the same.
concepts.why: The answer says < and <= behave the same with no condition, but they give different results when r equals sum exactly (for example r = 0.1 picks a different index), and it gives no boundary reasoning.
The answer says nothing about sum being built up as a running total.
The answer says nothing about statements or the order they run in.

concepts.quote: r <= sum would work the same.
concepts.why: This matches the listed wrong rule that the boundary test can be inclusive or exclusive interchangeably, and it doesn't note that the two differ when r lands exactly on a boundary (the zero-probability case) or answer what next is.
